surprises.description: AWI’s adjusted diluted EPS grew 10%, well below the preview’s implied 16.6% growth and $2.39 consensus. That implies roughly $2.26 per share, a material shortfall against the estimate.

The company lowered its adjusted EBITDA growth outlook to 8–10% from 9–12%, despite the preview’s expectation that the existing full-year guide would be narrowed rather than cut. The reduction reflects a weaker profit outlook than the preview’s expected H2 acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered the adjusted EBITDA growth guidance to 8-10% (from 9-12%), citing the highest input cost inflation since 2022 and tariff impacts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance: Adj. EBITDA $605–620M (+9–12%)”; the base case expected guidance to be “narrowed rather than raised.”

surprises.description: Freight inflation was running at roughly 20%, above the preview’s mid-teens expectation. Total input cost inflation was at the high end of mid-single digits, adding more cost pressure than the preview’s setup anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total input cost inflation is now tracking at the higher end of mid-single digits, led by roughly 20% freight inflation with diesel above $6 per gallon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “mid-teens freight inflation” and said it would “weigh more heavily in H2.”

surprises.description: Mineral Fiber’s full-year sales growth outlook was about 6.5%, slightly above the preview’s roughly 6% target, but management now expects full-year EBITDA margin to be roughly flat because of mix headwinds. That margin outlook is weaker than the preview’s emphasis on AUV as the support for the segment’s margin story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mineral Fiber full-year net sales growth was cut to approximately 6.5% (1 point volume, 5.5% AUV) with full-year EBITDA margin now expected roughly flat versus the prior year due to mix headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Mineral Fiber AUV — FY target ~+6%”; the preview called it “the entire margin story.”

surprises.description: Architectural Specialties outperformed the preview’s Q3 segment model: total sales rose 22% versus an expected 19% increase, and margin reached 19.4% versus the modeled 18.9%. Organic growth was a strong 16%, even though acquisitions continued to dilute margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Architectural Specialties delivered record organic growth of 16% (total net sales +22%) and expanded adjusted EBITDA margin 60 basis points to 19.4%, though acquisitions were dilutive to margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q3 segment model put Architectural Specialties at “~$180M (+19%) at ~18.9% margin.”

surprises.description: AWI raised full-year net sales growth guidance to 10–11% from 9–11%, helped by lifting the Architectural Specialties growth outlook to 18–19% from 15–17%. The higher AS outlook more than offset lower contributions from recent acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net sales guidance was raised slightly to 10-11%, driven by AS segment growth now expected at 18-19% (up from 15-17%), offset by lower contributions from recent acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed full-year net sales guidance of “$1,770–1,800M (+9–11%)” and described the base case as guidance being narrowed.

surprises.description: Canadian customers accelerated purchases ahead of anticipated tariffs, creating a timing-related shift toward lower-AUV channels. The preview discussed tariff costs and refunds but did not flag this pull-forward and mix effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Canadian customers accelerated purchases ahead of anticipated tariffs, driving a timing-related mix shift toward lower-AUV channels that is expected to moderate by year-end.”

surprises.description: Sales of ceiling and DynaMax structural grid products into data centers had already exceeded their full-year revenue plans. The preview highlighted data-center wins and asked for revenue or pipeline quantification, but did not anticipate that sales would be ahead of plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Both ceiling and DynaMax structural grid data center sales exceeded full-year revenue plans.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said investors wanted the data-center opportunity “quantified (revenue or pipeline dollars, not just ‘wins up X%’).”
